newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury names two members of advisory council.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury names two members of advisory council.

text.p: The British Treasury announced the appointment of Chris Wales, a tax partner at Arthur Andersen, and Paul Gregg of the Centre for Economic Performance as the first members of its new Council of Economic Advisers.
It said they would be "policy advisers to work alongside the Treasury teams dealing with, respectively, taxation and employment."

Treasury officials said there were no immediate plans to announce any other appointments to the new Council, which may eventually comprise up to six people. There will be no chairman and the council is intended to complement the work of Treasury staff, injecting outside expertise.
The Council will replace the Panel of Independent Forecasters, known as the "Wise Men," which advised the previous Conservative government.

"The Council of Economic Advisers is made up of individual policy experts who will bring their specialist experience to work alongside individual Treasury teams focussing on the government's key policy priorities," the Treasury said in a statement.

Wales moves from his position as tax partner at Arthur Andersen, for whom he has worked in both Britain and Sweden. His work has included projects involving financing structures and products, securitisation, cross-border leasing, acquisition finance and related structures, and treasury management, the Treasury said.

Gregg will continue to work part-time at the Centre for Economic Performance at the London School of Economics, where he is a senior research associate. His research areas include the dynamics of the British labour market.
